claims.text: SemiAnalysis's announcement said seven months had passed since Nvidia's CEO "said that TPU & Trainium would never come to InferenceX", and that both were now on InferenceX/AgentX, "the industry standard for inference benchmarking"[^1].

On the Dwarkesh Podcast on 15 April 2026 he said "Dylan's InferenceMAX is sitting out there for everybody to use, and not one… TPU won't come, Trainium won't come", and he added "I would welcome Trainium to demonstrate their 40% that they claim all the time"[^2].
When the benchmark launched in October 2025, Nvidia's own blog had said "NVIDIA Blackwell swept the new SemiAnalysis InferenceMAX v1 benchmarks"[^34].
The first post gave 1.2x to 2.5x, a later one 1.5–2.5x "at release" versus "equivalent NVIDIA GPUs"[^1,3].
Press accounts citing SemiAnalysis describe a Trainium3 UltraServer delivering "up to 2.28x better performance per dollar" than GB300 NVL72, B300 and MI355X.
It says Trainium3 with vLLM "is better than every other accelerator besides Vera Rubin across the entire TCO versus p90 interactivity curve"[^6].
It treats SemiAnalysis's runs as a third-party audit of results Google submitted itself[^32].
Vendors have also fought over its rules before: a warmup step in Nvidia's submission was banned for everyone after AMD queried it[^37].

At the operating point where Trainium3's lead peaks (about 246–250 tokens per second per user at P90), a reading of the dashboard reports about 9,266 total tokens per chip-second for Trainium3 and about 8,942 for GB300 NVL72[^5].
Crypto Briefing independently describes the same point as "only a marginal 4% performance lead"[^4].
The modeled hourly costs are $1.05 per chip for Trainium3 and $2.31 for GB300[^3,4].
At 20 tokens per second per user, TPUv7 produced 9,364 tokens per second per chip against 8,903 for B200, about 5% more, yet "50.4% more tokens per dollar"[^7].
Trainium3 has "only 17% the theoretical FP4 flops as Blackwell Ultra (2,517 TFLOPS versus 15,000 TFLOPS)" and "61% of the bandwidth at about 30% the TCO"[^6].
AgentX replays opt-in Claude Code sessions whose median request is about 142,000 input tokens and 444 output tokens[^28,5].
Google rates it at 4,614 FP8 TFLOPS and 7.37 TB/s per chip[^29], less bandwidth than GB300's 8 TB/s[^10]
The topology that wins on cost also costs latency: P90 time to first token was 4.5 seconds for Trainium3 against 1.8 seconds for GB300 at the comparison point[^4,5].
The reported points are 1.98x at about 140 tokens per second per user, 2.18x at about 190, 2.28x at about 250 and 2.01x at about 350[^3].
There Trainium3 reaches about 31,045 tokens per chip-second while GB300 reaches about 63,647, so GB300 does roughly twice the work per chip.
"The previously discussed 50% to 96% advantage applies to this datapoint specifically, rather than every latency target," the September article states.
Inferact reports "over 700 tokens/s with speculative decoding, compared with 452 tokens/s on GB200"[^31].
Its glossary defines two bases. "Internal TCO is the hourly cost of a chip to the company that designs and operates it".
Vera Rubin's $3.61 comes from the GLM-5.3 Rubin preview and a commentary reading of the dashboard's internal basis[^5,12].
Switching Ironwood from external to internal moves its lead over B300 from 96.0% to 130.2%[^9].
On that basis Vera Rubin delivers 3.3x Trainium3's tokens per dollar at 273 tokens per second per user[^5].
The firm says its rates draw on monthly surveys of "100+ gpu clouds"[^8].
On AWS's own list, a B300 accelerator-hour costs 7.2x a Trainium2 accelerator-hour ($16.146 against $2.235)[^13].
It says Trn2 offers "30-40% better price performance than GPU-based EC2 P5e and P5en instances", which are H200 machines[^15].
On the Q1 2026 call Andy Jassy said Trainium2 "has about 30% better price-performance than comparable GPUs" and that Trainium3 is "30-40% more price-performant than Trainium2"[^21].
SemiAnalysis's own September article put 3-year rental at "over $8.5/hr/chip for Rubin and $5/hr/chip for Blackwell Ultra NVL72" in July 2026[^11].
Spot asks on Vast.ai, collected by this site's own price lane on 27 November, had median rentable prices of $10.63 per GPU-hour for B300 and $9.06 for B200[^18].
CoreWeave lists GB200 NVL72 at $42.00 per four-GPU instance on demand, $10.50 per GPU, and advertises "up to 60% discounts" for commitments[^17].
Azure's retail API prices an ND GB200 v6 VM in East US at $108.16 an hour pay-as-you-go[^19].
Secondary reports put Ironwood at $12.00 per chip-hour on demand in Iowa, $8.40 on a one-year commitment and $5.40 on three years[^16].
The same report cites a SemiAnalysis estimate that Anthropic's contract rate is "roughly $1.60 per TPU-hour", about one-seventh of list[^16].
On that basis it gives Trainium3 a 73.5% profit margin against 53% for GB300 with SGLang at 135 tokens per second per user[^6].
On Kimi K3, "VR200 delivers 4.3x to 5.6x TPUv7"[^8].
A GLM-5.3 preview reported Vera Rubin NVL72 at 9.11x GB300's tokens per dollar at 200 tokens per second per user, priced at $3.61 against $2.31 per chip-hour[^12].
On GLM, "at 100 tok/s/user, GB300 and GB200 FP4 deliver 3.6x and 3.5x the tokens per dollar of TPUv7"[^8].
Nvidia reported GAAP gross margin of 74.8% for the quarter ended 25 October 2026, on revenue of $115.8 billion, $107.6 billion of it from data center[^41].
On Broadcom's fiscal Q3 call, its semiconductor segment gross margin was given as about 56.7%[^43].
It estimated Ironwood's all-in cost of ownership at about 44% below a GB200 server for Google, and up to about 30% below GB200 and 41% below GB300 for external customers after Google's markup[^44].
He also said "the majority and most of Bedrock today is being run on top of Trainium"[^22].
Huang disputed the margin arithmetic on Dwarkesh: "Nvidia's margin is 70%, let's say. But ASIC margins are 65%. What are you really saving?"[^2].
Its Q4 guidance steps down to 71–72%, and on the 17 November call interim CEO Colette Kress called Q4 "our bottom"[^41,42].
Kress took over when Huang resigned on 12 November, which is why SemiAnalysis's post called him "NVIDIA's former and current CEO"[^40,1].
Anthropic agreed to use up to one million TPUs, with "well over a gigawatt" online in 2026, and described "a diversified approach that efficiently uses three chip platforms"[^23].
It also committed to up to 5 GW of Trainium capacity and more than $100 billion of AWS spending over ten years[^24].
OpenAI committed to "approximately 2 gigawatts of Trainium capacity through AWS"[^26].
Anthropic also signed $30 billion with Azure for up to 1 GW of Nvidia Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems, alongside up to $10 billion of Nvidia investment[^25].
On Alphabet's Q3 call, Google Cloud said nearly 100 customers use TPUs and guided to "a meaningful revenue ramp in 2027" for TPU system sales[^35].
InferenceX's throughput side runs as public GitHub Actions workflows, with configs committed to the repo[^33].
A third-party profile found no editorial-independence policy on its site[^39].
